message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value (standard conditions) | Notes |
|----------|-----------------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in nucleus |
| **Symbol** | H | |
| **Common isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) | Deuterium used in heavy water; tritium is radioactive |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes |
| **Molecular formula** | H₂ (diatomic gas) | Most stable form at room temperature |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (120.95 K) | Extremely low; boils near absolute zero |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at very low temperatures |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | Lightest element; less dense than air |
| **Enthalpy of formation (ΔH_f°)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) | |
| **Standard entropy (S°)** | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (for H₂ gas) | |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | Energy to remove one electron from H atom |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV | Energy to remove second electron from H⁺ (not applicable for neutral H₂) |
| **Electron affinity** | 0.754 eV | Energy released when adding an electron to H atom |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements |
| **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) | For H₂ gas |
| **Thermal conductivity** | 0.1805 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) | High relative to other gases |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂); reacts with halogens (forming HX) | Highly reactive as a reducing agent |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Weak acid (HX) in aqueous solution; weak base (forming OH⁻) | In water, H₂ + 2OH⁻ ⇌ H₂O + H₂O₂ |
| **Isotopic effects** | Deuterium substitution shifts vibrational frequencies (~√(m_H/m_D)) | Used in kinetic isotope studies |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) | Classic hydrogen spectrum |

### Summary
- **Lightest element**: atomic mass ≈ 1 u, density ≈ 0.09 g L⁻¹.
- **Highly reactive**: forms compounds with almost all non‑metals; acts as a strong reducing agent.
- **Low boiling/melting points**: remains gaseous under most Earth conditions.
- **High electronegativity**: attracts electrons strongly, making it a good oxidizing agent in many reactions.
- **Isotopic variants**: protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive, β‑emitter).

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, influencing its role in chemistry, astrophysics, and energy applications.
